title: Buying a C-melody saxophone from Art Beam
summary: In April 1923 he buys a saxophone from the white music dealer Art Beam, forced to view it on the back porch, and watches white pupils run the scale.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: In the meantime I was falling in love -- had fallen in love with music. Come April in 1923, I told my dad I wanted to buy a saxophone. My dad says, "Well, if you want to buy a saxophone, Hayes, then go ahead. It's pretty expensive but if you think you can make it, go ahead. I'll help you." I went to a gentleman named Art -- Mr. Art Beam. Mr. Art Beam was a musician, and he sold instruments. And I had to go to see my horn and go on the back porch. He didn't invite me into his
house. I had to go in the back of the back porch to see this horn.

And I can remember it was a Holten horn. It wasn't exactly new, but it looked like new. And he charged me $151.60 for that horn. I gave him a down payment of $50.00. And my father stood for the horn and told him we would pay for it in a few months.

And in the meantime he asked me to come inside in order to sign some papers. This I did. While inside he was teaching some of the white kids how to play the saxophone, and I noticed the kids running the scale over the saxophone, as they would start at the low key C and run up to middle C on the horn. I didn't know what C was. I called that 'doe.' Doe, re, mi, fa, so, la, ti, doe. Because I had been taught that in high school. I didn't know the difference between instrumental music and vocal music.
